items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: I played a couple of film scores with him, played some incidental music for a Beckett play that he wrote for tympani and double bass.

ctx.x: Philip Glass was in Juilliard when I was there and he liked to jam. He had a house in Chinatown that he paid $65 a month rent. It was like a pretty, frame house, ramshackle, and we’d play down there once in a while. I had a motorcycle and I went down with the © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

bass on a motorcycle and we would play down there. And then later on you know what happened with him, he got very big. I played a couple of film scores with him, played some incidental music for a Beckett play that he wrote for tympani and double bass. And Beckett had instructed that there be no music for this play, I forget the name of the play. So he wrote tympani and bass. I guess that’s not music.
